role: OAuth, publication and media-integrity security reviewer

findings.problem: Final revalidation can accept stale project state. _manifest snapshots records before asynchronous asset/export checks and never rereads them afterward. Its fingerprint can therefore match the approval even when the episode changed during validation, allowing the public update.
findings.reproduction: Approve episode version 1. Pause _export during the final _fetch beforeSend revalidation, save episode version 2 through the existing episode-update route, then release _export. An in-memory probe using the real _manifest/_revalidate/_fetch methods confirmed that the injected public-update transport was invoked despite current version 2.
findings.correction: After the last asynchronous check, reread and compare all approval-bound record identities, versions and rights/provenance against the validated snapshot immediately before dispatch. Reject intervening changes with 409. Add a regression that edits the episode while final export validation is pending.

findings.problem: Approval invalidation prevents reconciliation of an already-known remote video. resume rejects before scheduling readback, and _drive repeats the same gate at line 470. An uncertain public transition consequently becomes unrecoverable through the supported reconciliation path after an episode/workflow edit.
findings.reproduction: Let a public update have an uncertain result with videoId persisted, then edit the episode before resuming. Revalidation rejects the stale approval, so no videos.list readback occurs. An in-memory control-flow probe confirmed zero readback attempts and resume returning 409.
findings.correction: Permit read-only reconciliation of the persisted session/video identity independently of approval freshness. Report observed visibility alongside stale-approval status; require current approval before any further upload or visibility-changing effect.

findings.problem: Resumable identities share one encrypted read-modify-write document, but privateQueue serializes only one service instance. Concurrent instances can overwrite each other's saved session URLs, losing the recovery identity that must be retained before transferring bytes.
findings.reproduction: Run two PublicationService instances against the same store, as anticipated by _upload's cross-process claim handling. Concurrently persist sessions for different intents. Both can read the previous document before either writes; the last write removes the other entry. An in-memory probe of the real _private method retained only intent-b.
findings.correction: Persist each intent's encrypted recovery state in a separate private-runtime record, or protect the entire shared-document transaction with cross-process locking/CAS. Add a concurrent-instance persistence regression.
